title: Variables for siting a new outpatient clinic

items.text: Demand and need in the catchment: population size, growth, age mix, disease burden and unmet need
paraphrases: Patient demand in the catchment area: population growth, age mix and unmet need.
Projected visit volume based on demographics and disease burden.
Community need assessment for primary and urgent care.

items.text: Payer mix and reimbursement: Medicaid/uninsured share determines revenue per visit and financial sustainability
paraphrases: Payer mix (commercial vs Medicaid vs uninsured) and resulting reimbursement.
Share of uninsured / self-pay patients drives financial sustainability.
Reimbursement rates differ sharply by site because of insurance mix.

items.text: Access: travel time, public transit, parking, walkability and hours for the target population
paraphrases: Travel time and transit access for the target population.
Accessibility: bus lines, parking and walkability.
Drive-time and public transportation to the site.

items.text: Competition and cannibalization: competitor capacity nearby, and patients pulled from our own existing clinic/hospital rather than new patients
paraphrases: Cannibalization: Site C would mostly draw patients from our own nearby clinic and hospital.
Competitor urgent care across the street and existing capacity nearby.
Incremental volume vs patients shifted from our existing sites.

items.text: Workforce: ability to recruit and retain physicians, nurses and staff willing to work at that site
paraphrases: Workforce: can we recruit physicians, nurses and MAs to that location?
Staffing availability and retention at each site.
Labor market for clinicians in the area.

items.text: Regulatory and zoning approvals: zoning/permitted use, permitting, licensing and timelines for medical/imaging use
paraphrases: Zoning and permits for medical and imaging use of the building.
Regulatory approvals and licensing timelines.
Land-use entitlements and code compliance for a clinic with X-ray.

items.text: Total real-estate and build-out cost: rent, lease terms, renovation, imaging shielding and time to open
paraphrases: Total occupancy cost: rent, lease terms and the cost of renovating the bank building.
Build-out cost including X-ray shielding and time to open.
Capital and construction cost differences across the sites.

items.text: Referral and downstream flows: links to the hospital, specialists, imaging and lab; keeping patients in-network
paraphrases: Referral flows to our hospital and specialists (downstream revenue and continuity).
Keeping patients in-network rather than leaking to competitors.
Care coordination with the hospital and specialists.

items.text: Mission and equity: serving underserved neighborhoods, community benefit obligations of a non-profit, health disparities
paraphrases: Mission and equity: Site B serves an underserved, low-income neighborhood.
Community-benefit obligations as a non-profit health system.
Impact on health disparities in the region.

items.text: Site physical suitability: size, layout, visibility, ADA accessibility, safety, signage and room for walk-in flow
paraphrases: Physical suitability: layout, square footage, ADA access and visibility.
Visibility and signage for a walk-in urgent care.
Building safety and security, especially for evening hours.

items.text: Growth and flexibility: room to expand, future population shifts, lease flexibility/exit options
paraphrases: Room to expand later and lease flexibility.
Future population growth and long-term scalability of each site.
Exit options if volumes disappoint.

items.text: Hazard and continuity risks: flood zone, disaster exposure, utility reliability
paraphrases: Flood zone and natural hazard exposure of each site.
Disaster resilience and utility reliability.
Climate risk at the site.

items.text: Strategic fit and partnerships: employers, schools, community organizations, the system's network strategy and payer contracts (value-based care)
paraphrases: Strategic fit with the system's network gaps and value-based contracts.
Partnerships with employers, schools and community organizations.
Does the site fill a white space in our network?
